gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-gujarati: Sharp, neon-bright angles up top, with every stroke ending at the same measured thickness in Megrim. Noto Sans Gujarati takes the quieter side, its curved strokes stopping short of turning inward, and that gentleness is the best thing about the match.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-gunjala-gondi: Megrim draws its letters like tube-shaped neon glass, angular and futuristic, with a c bent open like a paperclip. Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi follows in chunky, crayon-tall lowercase with cut-back terminals, so the glow above gets a sturdy footing below.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-gurmukhi: Angular and futuristic, with curves that never thin out at the turns. Noto Sans Gurmukhi sits underneath in a plain sans, its terminals pointing outward like tongs, and gives that sharp heading something steadier to lean on.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-hanunoo: Stencil-cut and angular, Megrim holds a constant weight through every channel of its letters. Noto Sans Hanunoo then fills most of the line height with open-ended lowercase, and the sans-serif body feels friendlier beside it.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-hebrew: Noto Sans Hebrew reads with a big, dominant midsection and wide gaps at its curves. Megrim sits above it, angular and futuristic, its thin-looking letters carrying no thinner parts, so the sans-serif body gets a sleek, sharp-edged lead.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-hk: Futuristic and angular, Megrim looks drawn with one pen tip, each glyph kept simple and clean. Noto Sans HK, a plain sans, lifts its brush ends away and sits quietly under it.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-imperial-aramaic: Noto Sans Imperial Aramaic has a friendly, approachable look, its c ends pointing apart like open pincers. And Megrim, with stroke contrast of exactly none, would make a longer stretch of text feel like a calm reply to its angular, futuristic heading.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-inscriptional-pa: Clean lines run through both fonts, from Megrim's angular heading with stroke ends as wide as the middle to the big open eyes of Noto Sans Inscriptional Parthian. Their strongest quality is crisp, uncluttered shape.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-jp: Modern in feel, Megrim is angular and futuristic, with no hairlines anywhere in its alphabet, while Noto Sans JP has a very tall x-height. Its curves sweep open, so a longer read feels easy.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-kaithi: Flat, single-weight linework defines Megrim, a futuristic, angular heading whose c opens like a bent paperclip. Noto Sans Kaithi, a plain sans with an open e channel, fills the line like capitals, and the strongest quality is how neatly they contrast.
